Before a launch, a short go/no-go question to every group the launch affects: are you ready? A "no" pauses the launch, not the release. No reply counts as yes.

- **Definition:** [Glossary: Launch, Readiness check](/system/glossary)
- **How it works:** [12 Build, release and enable](/system/build-release-and-enable)
- **Owner:** product owner
- **Links to:** [Deliverable](/templates/deliverable), [Release notes](/templates/release-notes)

## Template

| Field | What goes here |
|---|---|
| What is launching | Deliverable name and one-line benefit |
| Who gets it | Beta group or everyone |
| When | Date and time |
| Groups asked | Each affected group, with a one-line note on how it affects them |
| Reply by | Deadline. No reply counts as yes |
| Comms plan | Internal note timing, external note timing, guides, training dates |
| Result | Each group's reply, and the go/no-go decision |

## DMV example

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| What is launching | Online vehicle renewal: residents can renew registration online in about five minutes |
| Who gets it | Beta group of 25 residents, invited by letter |
| When | First Monday of week 9 |
| Groups asked | Field office supervisors in the two pilot offices (customers may arrive having started online). Contact center (calls about the beta). Web content team (help pages). Technical operations (monitoring). |
| Reply by | Thursday of week 8 |
| Comms plan | Internal note the Friday before; external note at launch; counter guide and two 30-minute sessions in week 8 |
| Result | Contact center: no, their scripts don't cover beta users yet. Others: yes. Launch moved one week to Monday of week 10 while scripts were written. The release itself was already in production. |
